newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-AMBROSE GIVES WINDIES A LIFT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AMBROSE GIVES WINDIES A LIFT.

text.p: Curtly Ambrose struck an early blow for West Indies to give India's batsmen food for thought at lunch on the second day of the third test at Kensington Oval on Saturday.

The Indians had reached 42-1 at the interval in reply to West Indies' 298 all out, but the loss of opener V.V. Laxman underlined the familiar threat of Ambrose on a pitch with more bounce than in the previous two tests.

Ambrose, who had earlier contributed 37 to help century-maker Shivnarine Chanderpaul lift West Indies towards 300, hit the top of Laxman's off-stump with a full-length delivery with the Indian total on a mere 23.

The Indians responded positively enough with 15 runs coming in the last over before lunch, Navjot Sidhu hitting three fours off Mervyn Dillon to reach 26 not out, but the pitch still offered plenty of encouragement to the West Indian pacemen.
Resuming on 240 for seven after Friday's rest day, West Indies added an additional 58 runs in 65 minutes in the morning.
Chanderpaul scored 35 of them to remain unbeaten on 137 including 13 fours. Venkatesh Prasad trapped last man Dillon lbw for a duck to return figures of five for 82 in 31.4 overs.
